_doc: Register of DAST findings that are real, reproduced, and awaiting a product decision (W2.4). Keyed by the finding's stable `pinKey` in scripts/security/dast-scan.mjs. A finding whose key is listed here is REPORTED by `bun run test:dast` without failing the lane, because its current behaviour is asserted byte-for-byte by the unit judges in scripts/security/dast-scan.test.mjs: the day the product changes, that assertion and this register must be revisited together. A finding whose key is NOT listed fails the lane. Removing an entry is how a fix gets locked in — never add one to go green. Each entry names the tracking issue; a placeholder `issue: 0` means the bug still has to be filed (the scanner prints a warning until it is a real number).

header.boundary-response-nosniff.note: packages/server/src/engine/http/http-server.ts writes its three transport-boundary JSON responses directly — 400 invalid_host (:301), 401 unauthorized (:353), 500 internal_server_error (:287) — with res.end(JSON.stringify(...)) and never sets `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. Every response that flows through the route handlers DOES set it (sendJson in engine/http/http-utils.ts:35), as do the web-ui shell (serve/web-ui-server.ts:158) and connections routes. The three boundary bodies are fixed server strings with no user-reflected content, so the sniffing exposure is low, but the omission is an inconsistency with the posture the same codebase holds everywhere else, not a documented decision. Product fix: route the boundary responses through a helper that stamps nosniff (or set it once alongside the CORS headers in route()). Out of scope for the DAST harness slice that found it.
